title: Permanent Wave (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word cabaret storytelling 128bpm warm upright bass brushed snare dry deadpan vocal absurdist comedy
lyrics:
[Intro - dry lounge piano, storytelling mode]
Now I'm going to tell you a story
About a rabbit on a country road
The afternoon was warm and golden
And the rabbit had nowhere particular to go

[Verse 1]
A car came round the corner slowly
Not fast, not dangerous, just enough
The rabbit sat there slightly dazed
Just staring at the sky, a little rough

The driver stopped and got out quietly
Looked at the rabbit lying in the sun
Searched the boot for something useful
And found an aerosol from 1981

[Pre-Chorus]
Read the label, couldn't quite make it out
Thought it might be worth a go
Gave the rabbit a generous coating
And waited to see what the results would show

[Chorus]
Permanent wave, permanent wave
The rabbit got up and started to wave
Ran off waving, stopped, and waved again
Waved from the distance, waved round the bend
Permanent wave, permanent wave
Still waving now, somewhere down that lane

[Verse 2]
The driver stood there on the roadside
Watching the rabbit disappear from view
Still waving as it crossed the paddock
Still waving as it came around loop two

The driver picked the can up slowly
Turned it over, read the small print there
One product, two remarkable features
Instant restoration, and a permanent wave of the hair

[Bridge - spoken, deadpan]
Hair Restorer
With Permanent Wave
The rabbit was fine
Remarkably well-groomed
Still waving

[Chorus]
Permanent wave, permanent wave
The rabbit got up and started to wave
Ran off waving, stopped, and waved again
Waved from the distance, waved round the bend
Permanent wave, permanent wave
Still waving now, somewhere down that lane

[Outro - piano, gently fading]
If you're ever on a country road
And the afternoon is warm and slow
Check your boot for solutions
You never quite know how the story goes
Permanent wave
